summary: Aloysius Pieris (1934–2026) was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sacred Heart College, University of London, Pontifical Theological Faculty of Southern Italy, University of Sri Lanka, and Tilburg University, and founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre.
Alubomulle Sumanasara (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë (born 1964) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford and Harvard University. He has held academic posts at the City University of New York, the University of California, Santa Cruz, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Alvappillai Veluppillai (1936–2015) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied under K. Kanapathypillai at the University of Peradeniya and Thomas Burrow at the University of Oxford, holding posts at Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University.

Amalananda Ghosh (1910–1981) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He served as Director General of Archæology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and held posts at UNESCO and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.
Amalia Pezzali (born 1928) is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under T. R. V. Murti and Michel Hulin.

Amanda K. Goodman works in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez, Jr., and later took up a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Nath Pandeya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who held positions at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history/archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder, as well as Rahul Sankrityayan, Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amaranatha Jha (1897–1955) studied at Muir Central College, where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).
Amarasvar Thakur was an Indology scholar who served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series and held an attested post at the University of Calcutta in 1936.

Amartya Sen (born 1933) is a philosopher and economist. Educated at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge, he held posts at Jadavpur University, the University of Delhi, the London School of Economics, and Harvard University.

Amber D. Carpenter is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Her teachers included M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte, and she has held positions at the University of St Andrews, the University of York, and Yale-NUS College.
Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate from the University of Oxford. She has held posts at Central Michigan University and Naropa University.

Amin Sweeney (1938–2010) was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of London. He served as a lecturer and professor at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (1970–1977) and later chaired the Department of South and Southeast Asian Studies at UC Berkeley.
Amita Chatterjee (born 1950) is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amy Heller (born 1951) is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist. She studied at INALCO and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald, and held posts at the CNRS, the University of Rome, SOAS, and INALCO.

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She received her PhD from Columbia University (~2002–2008) and was appointed assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2014.

Amy Sims Miller is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her BA at Wesleyan University and her MA and PhD at the University of Virginia, where she was supervised by David F. Germano.
